summary: Strengthen education finance and resource allocation skills with practical budgeting, costing, and funding tools. Enroll to improve how you plan and justify spe
lede: Education finance and resource allocation is the process of planning and distributing funding, staff time, and physical resources to support learning priorities. For professionals who manage education budgets, the course covers program-based budgeting, unit-cost analysis, allocation formula design, and scenario modeling to connect spending decisions with learning and equity goals.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who already work with education budgets, funding decisions, or resource planning and need to strengthen their ability to link spending to learning outcomes and equity goals.
modules: Unit Costs, Cost Analysis, and Value for Money
Funding Formulas and Resource Allocation Models
Managing Donor-Funded and Project-Based Education Finance
Digital Tools, Data Integration, and Dashboards
Governance, Accountability, and Reporting in Education Finance
prerequisites: This is an intermediate-level course designed for professionals already working with education budgets or financial decisions. You should have: (1) basic familiarity with budgeting concepts and financial terminology in an education or public-sector context, (2) experience reviewing or preparing simple budgets, grant proposals, or spending reports, and (3) working knowledge of spreadsheets such as Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets; no advanced modeling or coding is required. The course teaches program-based budgeting, unit cost analysis, and allocation modeling at an operational application level, with hands-on implementation limited to spreadsheet-based tools that you can reasonably apply in your own organization after the training.
